subject: Hybrid invoice ingest: envelope vs subject-token — decision and next steps
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@pixeldynamics.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
Cc: procurement@pixeldynamics.com
Date: 2026-03-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice submission for PixelDynamics - portal availability and template

Hi Jonas,

Quick intro — I'm Elena, procurement at PixelDynamics. We're working through vendor activation and our finance team asked whether Redwood expects suppliers to use the portal or whether email submission is an acceptable long-term option. Two constraints on our side: (1) our ERP currently can't integrate with new portals until the end of Q2, and (2) some of our suppliers need to send a single PDF invoice that references multiple POs across different payment entities.

Can you share the minimal CSV/CSV-like schema or subject-token conventions you prefer if we need to use email for the first 8–12 weeks? We want a deterministic subject line so our team can auto-route to the correct ledger/entity. Also curious about ACK latency (how quickly Redwood will respond with acceptance/validation), and whether you support PO-stamping (matching an incoming invoice to one or many POs).

I've attached a sample invoice PDF so you can see the structure we've been generating.

Thanks — Elena

Attachment: PD-invoice-sample.pdf (stub)

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@pixeldynamics.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodai.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodai.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice submission for PixelDynamics - portal availability and template

Hi Elena — thanks for the sample and context. Short answer: portal-first, email-backstop. Longer here so your ops folks can decide.

Portal-first (recommended)
- Best for idempotency, automatic PO match, and faster ACKs (near-real-time 1–2 mins for acceptance when payload validates).
- Allows multiple POs per invoice and explicit entity/ledger mapping during onboarding.

Email fallback (supported, recommended subject-token pattern)
- If portal isn't an option initially, use an email subject token that contains: [PD-ID] [Entity] [PO-list]. Example subject: "RDW-INVOICE PD-12345 ENT-US HQ PO:PO12345,PO12346". That format allows our ingest to route and pre-map entities.
- Attach a single PDF or a CSV where line items are enumerated. We prefer a minimal CSV schema for auto-processing. See attached redwood_minimal_invoice_schema.csv for the exact column names we program against.

PO stamping and matching
- We do PO-stamping on ingest when PO numbers are present and matchable. If PO list includes multiple entities across ledgers, include an explicit Entity token as in the example so we can assign lines correctly.

ACK SLAs
- Syntactic acceptance ACK: usually within 1–5 minutes for email-based ingestion during business hours.
- Semantic validation (tax/PO reconciliation) may be queued and you'll get a final acceptance email within 24 hours unless exceptions require manual review.

Operational asks from PixelDynamics to make email fallback smooth
1) Use the subject token pattern above (PD-<vendorID> optional if you supply vendorID during onboarding).
2) If the invoice references multiple POs across entities, add a short mapping in the email body like: "PO12345->ENT-US; PO12346->ENT-EU" so we can map quickly.
3) If you can, send a CSV along with the PDF (CSV primary for automated ingest, PDF as human-readable).

Attaching: redwood_minimal_invoice_schema.csv (stub) and a one-click onboarding form link; copying Vanessa and Kimberly to coordinate the onboarding form and entity mapping.

I'll schedule a short handoff with your team if helpful.

— Jonas

Attachment: redwood_minimal_invoice_schema.csv (stub)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@pixeldynamics.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
Cc: procurement@pixeldynamics.com
Date: 2026-03-06T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice submission for PixelDynamics - portal availability and template

Thanks Jonas — that's helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we roll to suppliers:

1) Our vendors will default to a single attached PDF. If we include the subject token (PD-22388 ENT-US PO:PO111,PO112) but no CSV, will Redwood still attempt PO-stamping from the subject token and PDF text? Or will that force manual review?

2) Is there a short, machine-readable onboarding handshake we can include in our vendor-facing instructions (for example, a single-line example subject and a tiny CSV header row) so our supplier helpdesk doesn't have to reformat when they email?

3) If we start with email fallback, what's the recommended cadence to migrate vendors onto the portal? We expect to migrate in waves over 4–6 weeks after portal enablement.

Elena

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodai.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodai.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Invoice submission for PixelDynamics - portal availability and template (internal next steps)

(Internal) Vanessa/Kim — PixelDynamics needs:
- A one-page vendor-facing instruction (single subject-token example + tiny CSV header) we can hand to suppliers as "email fallback instructions." Put this behind the onboarding form link and make it downloadable.
- Confirm ingest behavior when only PDF+subject token present: do we attempt automated OCR/PO match and what is the error-rate threshold before manual review? We should document caveats (POs embedded in PDF scanned images).
- Recommend migration cadence: propose 4-week pilot group -> 4–6 week broad rollout (aligns with Elena's expectation).

I created a draft onboarding-form link and included it in attachments for reference. Can you own the supplier PDF fallback artifact and a short Ops runbook for exception handling? I'll take the handoff meeting with PixelDynamics next week.

Thanks — Jonas

Attachment: onboarding-form-link.txt (contains https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-invoice-handshake-spec)
